subject: EdgeCommerce renewal: capacity uplift options & rate framing
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@edgecommerce.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - numbers & burst behavior

Thanks Sofia — quick context from our side. We’re planning to renew in September and want to increase our committed monthly token volume. Our last 90-day usage (attached) shows three predictable weekly spikes tied to promotional blasts. Two questions before we commit: (1) how will rate limits behave during a spike if we stay in the hosted plan (will requests get queued, throttled, or fallback to the next rate tier?), and (2) what’s the best short-term uplift path that doesn’t require a Private deployment?

We’re also tightening budget approvals, so a clear breakdown of incremental cost vs. burst credits would help.

—Sarah
EdgeCommerce, Head of AI Integrations
[Attachment: Edge-Usage-Report-Jun2027.csv]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - numbers & burst behavior

Hi Sarah — thanks for the usage file, that’s helpful. Short answers up front: during hosted-plan spikes we prioritize latency SLOs within the committed tier and then apply burst credits; if credits are exhausted we apply graceful rate limiting (HTTP 429) with a configurable fallback to a lower-capacity variant (model size or quantized variant).

Options for a smooth renewal (two paths we commonly recommend):

1) Tiered commit uplift (short-term, lowest friction): add a 30–50% uplift to your monthly commit and increase burst credits by a defined multiple. No infra changes; live on Hosted.

2) Reserved short-term Dedicated buffer (medium friction): reserve a small Dedicated pool for peak windows (weekday promos). Predictable throughput, slightly higher committed spend but fewer 429s.

I’ll loop Karthik to sketch the capacity and Marcus to propose pricing concessions for a 12-month amendment. Can you confirm the spike windows (days/times) and the peak tokens/min target you want covered?

—Sofia
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@edgecommerce.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - numbers & burst behavior

Hi Sarah, quick technical note from infra/SE side. Based on the CSV sample you sent, the worst observed 1-hour peak averages ~3.6x baseline token rate, with short sub-minute bursts up to ~6x. For Hosted we recommend either: (A) bump committed monthly tokens by 40% and double burst credits (we can quantify exact token buckets after a short ingestion), or (B) add a Dedicated burst pool sized to cover the 6x peaks for your promo windows.

Tradeoffs: option A is faster to approve and lowest ops overhead; you may still see occasional 429s at extreme microbursts. Option B reduces throttling risk but requires a 3–6 week provisioning lead time and a minimum monthly commitment.

I’ve attached a one-page capacity sketch and an estimated throughput profile. Happy to run this against additional sample days if you want more precision.

—Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity-sketch-Jul2027.pdf]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@edgecommerce.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 12-month amendment + promo burst credits

Sarah — based on Sofia and Karthik’s notes, here’s a commercial proposal that’s most aligned with your asks: 

- Increase committed monthly tokens by 45% (effective Sep 1)
- Double burst credits for the first 3 billing cycles post-renewal
- Maintain current per-token rates for the first 6 months, then move to the standard published rate (we’ll include a cap on month-to-month increases)
- Include one free Dedicated weekend buffer for two major promo weekends (provisioned as Hosted-reserved capacity)

We can formalize this as a 12-month amendment. I’ve attached the draft amendment (Proposal v1). If this looks good, we’ll prepare a DocuSign and reserve the promo weekend buffer immediately upon signature.

Open points: exact billable token definition for certain multi-part calls (we propose counting model input+output tokens; will include examples in the amendment).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed-Amendment-EdgeCommerce.pdf]

Thanks Marcus — the proposal looks reasonable and addresses our main concern (burst handling). Two small asks before legal signs: (1) clarify the token counting examples in the amendment (please include a short appendix with 3 example call types), and (2) confirm that the twice-doubled burst credits apply retroactively from the first post-renewal billing cycle rather than pro-rated.

If you can update the PDF with those two clarifications, I’ll route to our procurement and get signatures within 72 hours. We appreciate the weekend buffer inclusion — that was a deciding factor.

—Sarah
Head of AI Integrations, EdgeCommerce
